subject: Data fencing requirements — Dedicated vs Private VPC (next steps)
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@meditech.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Data fencing requirements — recap + clarifying questions

Elena / Alec — thanks for the call earlier today. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can prepare an options memo.

Summary from our side:
- Primary ask: confirm whether PHI-bound workloads must run in a fully customer-controlled network/premises (on-prem or private VPC with customer-managed control plane) versus being acceptable on Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool managed by Redwood) with strong logical isolation.
- Non-PHI inference (de-identified telemetry, analytics) may be OK on Dedicated if we can guarantee encryption at rest, tenant-level keys, and strict RBAC.
- Procurement timeline: you mentioned internal legal/procurement review in Feb.

Clarifying questions that will materially change the option set: 
1) For PHI, do you require physical/co-located hardware (on-prem) or is a VPC with customer-managed networking + KMS sufficient?
2) Is there a defined list of data fields you consider PHI (PII + lab IDs, patient identifiers, free text notes)? If you can share a short list we can map flows.
3) What are the minimum logging/audit requirements for served requests (full request payload vs metadata only)?
4) Any hard constraints on latency/SLO for PHI inference (e.g., <200ms p50)?

Next steps we propose: 
- We’ll draft two short options: (A) Dedicated capacity with tenant isolation + HSM-backed customer keys; (B) Private VPC / on-prem architecture with private control plane. Each option will include: expected timeline, high-level cost delta, security artifacts we’ll provide (SOC2, penetration test summary), and a short migration path if you want a staged approach.

Can you confirm the items above and attach the segmentation spec you mentioned? If you can send the PHI field list and the procurement timeline target date, we’ll prioritize this for your Feb procurement window.

Thanks — I’ll wait for the attachments and will follow up with a draft options memo by Friday next week.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Morales <elena@meditech.io>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: Alec Turner <alec.turner@meditech.io>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 17:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data fencing requirements — recap + clarifying questions

Thanks Sean — good recap. Quick answers inline, and I attached a rough segmentation spreadsheet (Meditech_Segmentation_Specs.xlsx).

1) PHI requirement: For anything that includes direct patient identifiers or full clinical notes we require customer-controlled network boundaries. That can be Private VPC with a customer-managed control plane in our VPC (preferred) or fully on-prem (possible, but heavier). Logical isolation on Dedicated is not sufficient for PHI.
2) PHI fields: patient name, DOB, MRN, SSN, full clinical notes, radiology reports with identifiers. Non-sensitive telemetry (de-identified vitals / aggregate metrics) can be served on Dedicated.
3) Auditing: we need full request/response logging retained for 365 days (encrypted at rest), plus immutable request IDs tied to our internal case IDs.
4) Latency: for PHI workloads we can tolerate higher latency (p95 < 1s) if it simplifies architecture; for user-facing flows (non-PHI) we want <200ms p50.

Procurement target: we need pricing + architecture by Jan 22 to include in the Feb procurement packet.

Attachments: Meditech_Segmentation_Specs.xlsx (contains field lists and tentative flow diagrams).

Appreciate the staged approach idea — we’re open to starting on Dedicated for non-PHI while we certify the Private VPC for PHI. Please include estimated engineering effort for the Private VPC setup (two-line summary).

Best,
Elena
Elena Morales
Head of Infrastructure & Security, Meditech Health

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Elena Morales <elena@meditech.io>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data fencing requirements — recap + clarifying questions

On Tue, Jan 13, 2026 at 2:05 PM Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com> wrote:
> Elena / Alec — thanks for the call earlier today. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can prepare an options memo.

Thanks for the notes. A few internal asks so we can produce the clean options memo Elena requested by Jan 22: 
- Sean: can you prepare two short sections (one paragraph each) that define what we mean by “tenant isolation” on Dedicated (kernel-level isolation, dedicated GPU pool, per-tenant KMS keys) and a short, high-level diagram for Private VPC mode (control plane placement, network egress, KMS ownership).
- Monica: can you pull the current SOC2/pen test summary and a one-paragraph note on what audit artifacts we can provide for Private VPC customers? I’ll use that in the memo.
- Elena: to be precise for procurement, can you confirm whether the 365-day retention requirement is for full payloads or metadata only? If full payloads, we’ll call that out as a high-cost driver.

Also proposing a hybrid path to present to Meditech: start with Dedicated for non-PHI and pilot Private VPC for a single model/flow that processes PHI. That reduces time-to-value while satisfying PHI constraints. If Meditech prefers, we can include an estimated delta in TCO between the two approaches (OPEX + set-up).

I’ll coordinate with the infra team to get sample latency numbers for a small LLM on Dedicated and a Private VPC deploy; Sean — please add those numbers to the memo.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Solutions Architecture, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Morales <elena@meditech.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Alec Turner <alec.turner@meditech.io>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data fencing requirements — recap + clarifying questions

Thanks — confirmed. PHI = patient identifiers, lab results with identifiers, and full clinical notes. For those flows we will require Private VPC with customer-managed control plane (we prefer that to full on-prem at first).

I uploaded the security questionnaire responses (Meditech_Security_Questions_Filled.pdf) to the Drive link and attached a copy here. Procurement asks two numbers from us:
- 1) Minimal viable Dedicated configuration pricing (monthly) to run non-PHI inference at expected scale (we’ll provide expected QPS in follow-up)
- 2) High-level one-time install + recurring TCO estimate for Private VPC (we don’t need line-item detail, just a band: low/medium/high).

Deadline: Jan 22 for the memo/pricing. If you can include an architecture sketch (1 slide) and a two-line install effort estimate (person-weeks) for Private VPC, that would be ideal.

We’ll review the segmentation spreadsheet and come back with small clarifying edits by EOD Friday.

Thanks — Elena

Attachments: Meditech_Security_Questions_Filled.pdf
